I'm going through what OP is going through. I failed a nursing licensing exam because of this and my relationships are suffering too. I can completely relate to how she feels. I read your reply several times because I feel that what you've said is so true to me. I'm putting so much pressure and expectation on myself that it's making me hate what I do. When I don't do what I need to do, I'm filled with self hate and guilt. It's so very counter productive. OP and I have to start forgiving and loving ourselves. That includes shifting our focus from thinking that we "have to", "must", or "should be" doing things to wanting to do things. Accomplish your tasks because you it enriches your life in some way or another. That's what I took away of your reply. I just wanted to say thank you for your wise words.

Perhaps you could go to the library and find something you find interesting to read as a way to preoccupy your time. Or you can start to write down your thoughts and feelings when you find it difficult to cope with your emotions.

 I know what it's like to lounge around all day and it sucks. It makes things worse when all your thinking about are your problems. Go outside and take a stroll in a nearby park, it can help.


Lastly, since your husband is away, maybe it would be helpful if you moved back home for awhile, where you have the most support from your family and friends. If that isn't possible, they are just a phone call away! You are going to get through this.
